claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start by beginning the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! To help you with your Child Benefit eligibility, I need to start by learning about your child/children.

**First, could you please tell me:**

1. **How many children are you claiming for?**
2. **What are their names and ages?**

This will help me determine which eligibility rules apply to your situation. Child Benefit has different requirements depending on whether children are:
- **Under 16 years old** (generally automatic eligibility)
- **16-19 years old** (must be in education or training)
- **20 years or older** (not eligible for Child Benefit)

Please provide your child/children's details and I'll guide you through the rest of the assessment.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
Hi, yes I'm interested in claiming Child Benefit and wanted to check if I'm eligible.

I have one child - Alex, who's 16 years old.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you have **one child, Alex, who is 16 years old**.

Since Alex is 16, I need to check whether he/she is in education or training, as this affects eligibility. Let me navigate to the next part of the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Now I need to check Alex's education status. **Can you tell me:**

**Is Alex currently:**
1. **In education or training?** (For example: secondary school, college, university, apprenticeship, etc.)
2. Or has Alex **recently left education/training?** (If so, approximately how long ago?)
3. Or **neither** (not in education/training and hasn't recently left)?

This is important because for 16-19 year olds, Child Benefit eligibility depends on their education or training status.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex isn't in any education or training at the moment. He left school a little while back and isn't doing any courses or anything like that right now.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. So Alex has left education/training but isn't currently in any education or training now.

I need to ask: **approximately how long ago did Alex leave school/education?** 

This is important because there's a specific time window - if Alex left very recently (within a certain period), there may still be extension eligibility to consider. Could you give me an approximate timeframe? For example:
- A few weeks ago?
- A few months ago?
- More than 6 months ago?

Let me also get the specific time limits so I can advise you properly.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good - I can see that there's a **20-week extension period** for young people who have recently left education or training. So if Alex left school within the last 20 weeks, there may still be eligibility.

**Can you tell me approximately when Alex left school?** For instance:
- Within the last few weeks?
- Within the last 2-3 months?
- Within the last 5 months?
- Or more than 5 months ago?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: It's been more than 5 months now since Alex left school.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Since Alex left school more than 5 months ago, that means Alex is now **outside the 20-week extension period** (which is approximately 5 months).

Let me navigate to determine the outcome based on this information.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'm sorry to inform you that based on the information you've provided, **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

**Here's why:**

Child Benefit eligibility for 16-19 year olds requires them to be in **approved education or training**. While there is a 20-week extension period after leaving education/training, Alex has now been out of education for **more than 5 months** (beyond the 20-week extension window).

**Key points:**
- Alex is 16 years old
- Alex left school more than 5 months ago
- Alex is not currently in any education, training, or apprenticeship
- The 20-week extension period has expired

**What could change this:**
If Alex were to enter an **approved education or training programme** (such as a course, apprenticeship, or vocational training), you could then reapply for Child Benefit. The approved programmes include qualifications like A-levels, T-levels, NVQs (Levels 1-3), BTEC qualifications, and other similar courses.

If you have any questions or if Alex's circumstances change, feel free to get back in touch!

Let me now provide you with the formal outcome:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Assessment Complete**

Unfortunately, you are **not eligible for Child Benefit** at this time for Alex.

If you'd like more information about getting Alex into education or training, you may wish to contact:
- Local education services
- Your local youth services
- Careers guidance services

Or if you have questions about this assessment, you can contact HMRC's Child Benefit team.

Although there is a 20-week extension period after leaving education/training, Alex left school more than 5 months ago, which exceeds this 20-week extension window. Therefore, Alex does not meet the qualifying criteria for Child Benefit.
